artifacts.summary: Research on the three gitignore/loose-file hygiene gaps: (A) the latex/build/ cruft is already fully covered by an existing generic build/ rule (review premise refuted by git check-ignore evidence, but adding an explicit rule is still worth doing for clarity); (B) /.pid is a confirmed, uncomplicated gap; (C) Challenge.lean is not a stray scratch file but the committed trust-boundary artifact of lean-challenge-snapshot.sh (the Comparator statement-pinning mechanism) -- it must be documented in ORGANISATION.md, not relocated to Boneyard/, which would break the mechanism.

memory_candidates.content: BimodalLogic's .gitignore line 3 is a bare, unanchored `build/` rule (intended for Lean's own build/ output per its comment) that also incidentally matches any directory literally named `build` anywhere in the tree, including latex/build/ and latex/subfiles/build/. Before adding a new gitignore rule for 'unignored' cruft, run `git check-ignore -v <path>` first -- a review/finding that assumes a path is unignored can be wrong if an existing generic/unanchored rule already covers it by coincidence.

BimodalLogic's root-level Challenge.lean is not loose scratch content: it is the git-committed output of `.claude/scripts/lean-challenge-snapshot.sh`, which pins a lean task's intended theorem STATEMENTS (bodies optionally `sorry`) as the trust boundary `lean-comparator-run.sh` checks an untrusted Solution.lean against. The script writes to `<project_root>/Challenge.lean` by design (default module name 'Challenge'), so each new snapshot-running task overwrites the previous working-tree copy -- the old content is never lost because it stays recoverable forever at its own commit SHA (recorded in that task's archived specs/{N}_{slug}/challenge/manifest.json), not in the working tree. Relocating or deleting the root file breaks the mechanism's precondition; the correct treatment when such a file is found undocumented is to document it (e.g. in ORGANISATION.md), never to archive/move it.
